message:
chore(release): 0.2.106 and APK 0.2.14 candidates -- built, not shipped

Candidates only. The operational signing key is still not embedded, nothing
is signed for release, nothing is published, nothing is installed, and
nothing is pushed.

New numbers rather than the 0.2.105 / 0.2.13 candidates that already exist,
because a great deal of work landed after those were built and reusing a
number would make two different binaries answer to one version.

The installer's payload is verified by reading the RT_RCDATA resources and
hashing the bytes, then comparing against the files the build produced --
nine of nine. A file name appearing in the binary is not evidence: the name
survives while the bytes go stale. Four of them failed on the first run and
that was my mapping, not the product; I had guessed the payload names. A
comparison against guessed names reports a defect in the list rather than in
the thing being checked.

The APK carries the same signer certificate as 0.2.13, the same package, and
versionCode 13 over 12.

Recorded with it: the approval linearises at SetEvent(ack), the owner is
checked immediately before that, and the gap between the two is not atomic
-- a sign-out landing inside it cannot recall an approval already sent, and
there is no cancellation after that point. Closing the window means putting
the check and the approval in one critical section, which is a general
synchronisation redesign and not this task. Writing the window down is the
honest thing available now.

And the unverified list is re-stated: several entries said "only possible in
the field" when the accurate phrase is "not run in this pass". TLS 1.2 is
enforced by construction but cannot be read back; a valid https exchange did
succeed through the product transport; the downgrade refusal is still
unobserved on the wire. The live NAS is not entirely unknown either -- the
TLS GET succeeded and the metadata was absent; what is unknown is the
backend's version.
